client_situation.text: The City of Colfax, California — a Sierra Nevada foothills town of just under 2,000 people in Placer County at the junction of Interstate 80 and State Route 174 — is the issuing body and sole beneficiary of this RFP.
The City runs on annual budgeted revenues of $6 million with 11 full-time employees (one position vacant) plus one part-time/seasonal/contract employee, and its fiscal year ends June 30.

The City currently uses Tyler Technologies' Fund Balance fund accounting software with modules for Accounts Payable (including 1099 filing, purchasing requisitions and purchase orders with approvals), Accounts Receivable, General Ledger, Payroll, Utility Billing and Business Licensing, and has five users.

The City is replacing its current system with a cloud-based accounting and financial reporting system because it wants a streamlined package that captures financial transactions systematically, supports budgeting and forecasting, produces reports and analysis for decision-making, and maintains auditable records.
The City's small staff size and single-vacancy headcount mean the selected vendor must carry substantial implementation and support workload rather than relying on City capacity.

goal.text: The City wants a cloud-based accounting and financial reporting software system plus complete support for initial implementation and ongoing services for all applications the selected vendor provides.
The City's stated go-live target is July 1, 2026, to align with the start of its new fiscal year, with the project starting soon after contract award and negotiation.

The scope is organized into four tasks: Task 1 Approach & Project Management Plan (weekly progress/budget/timeline meetings, dedicated project manager, audit and reporting expertise, recommended account structure), Task 2 Software Installation & Implementation (financial report writing, import of the prior 5 years of data, coordination with Accounting and IT to minimize disruption), Task 3 Staff Training During Implementation (personalized power-user training and manuals, at least one recorded session and manual for all staff, support for the first 12 months), and Task 4 Ongoing Technical Assistance & Support (automated updates and change notices, annual 1099/W-2 e-filing support, help desk or ticketing system).

Respondents must supply an implementation plan and timeline, describe support levels for implementation and for recurring licenses and services, name key implementation personnel, describe training by license level (in person, virtual or recorded), and describe the client engagement approach including use of an account manager.

Tab 1 requires a completed Attachment F "Software Abilities and Requirements" spreadsheet, identification of license types by level of use, a description of account number customization, disclosure of where other applications or vendors will be used, and the availability of virtual product demos.

success_criteria.text: Proposals are scored on four weighted criteria: 45% response to project goals and scope, 25% technical support during implementation and ongoing, 20% fee proposal and implementation schedule, and 10% information, qualifications and references.
Written questions are due July 31, 2025, the City posts its answers on www.colfax-ca.gov by August 14, 2025, and proposals are due August 28, 2025 at 4:00 PM PST.
Finalists are notified September 11, 2025, virtual finalist interviews (if needed) are held September 25, 2025, and selection and contract award are targeted for October 22, 2025.
Proposals must include at least three references for similar services with valid e-mail addresses, and a missing or invalid email may cause rejection of the proposal.
The City prefers at least one local referral that can host an in-person software demonstration.
The City may shortlist finalists for interviews with City leadership or select without interviews, and price proposals cannot be altered or modified during clarification.
The City may reject any proposal on fit, form, function or cost, may make separate awards for different items, may not award certain items, or may cancel the RFP entirely.

constraints.text: Proposals must be one signed original hard copy plus one digital copy, no more than 20 pages plus 2 pages for the cover letter and 5 pages for appendices, emailed to accounting@colfax-ca.gov with the subject line "Accounting and Financial Software Submission" and the hard copy received by the same August 28, 2025 4:00 PM PST deadline at Attn: Shanna Stahl, PO Box 702, Colfax, CA 95713 or 33 S. Main Street, Colfax, CA 95713.
Late proposals and FAX submissions will not be accepted or evaluated.

The City will not accept unlimited reimbursable expenses; all reimbursable expenses must be capped in the Attachment A price proposal, which must break out implementation fees, recurring fees, license fees, support costs during versus after implementation, and estimated costs for additional applications or vendors.
Respondents must submit Attachment C disclosing all work locations and any use of workers outside the United States, which the City will weigh for additional risks and costs before award.

Respondents must submit Attachment D Certification of Financial Condition (stable finances, unqualified audit opinion, no IRS or government liens, current on taxes, no disqualifying litigation) and Attachment E proof of insurance including workers compensation and commercial general liability.
Attachment G requires documentation of measures protecting financial data and the secure access controls implemented.

Attachment F is an Excel spreadsheet the City provides as a separate document that must be completed and returned with the submission, and the City's standard contract for services is a separate document respondents must obtain and review.

Any additional or modified terms and conditions submitted with a proposal will be rejected and not evaluated, and objections to the City's terms stated in the proposal will be disregarded or cause rejection, so exceptions must be raised as written questions by July 31, 2025.

chunk_summaries.summary: The document is a Request for Proposals from the CITY OF COLFAX titled "Accounting and Financial Reporting Software". Date of Issue: July 1, 2025. Submission Deadline: Thursday, August 28, 2025 at 4:00 PM PST. The chunk begins a section directing all inquiries concerning this RFP to a contact (contact details not included in this chunk).

The City of Colfax (City) is issuing this Request for Proposals (RFP) to solicit comprehensive proposals for the acquisition and implementation of a cloud-based accounting and financial reporting software system. The scope includes complete support for both initial implementation and ongoing services for all applications provided by the selected software vendor. Key objectives: a streamlined software package capturing financial transactions systematically and efficiently, including budgeting and forecasting capabilities; ability to generate reports and analyze data to support informed decision-making; ability to maintain auditable records and documentation for future reference; dedicated technical support during implementation and throughout annual contract renewals. The City currently uses Fund Balance fund accounting software from Tyler Technologies, with modules for Accounts Payable (with 1099 filing capability, purchasing requisitions, and purchase orders with approvals), Accounts Receivable, General Ledger, Payroll, Utility Billing, and Business Licensing, and currently has five users.

The client is the City of Colfax, California, a small city in the Sierra Nevada foothills of Placer County with a population just under 2,000, located at the junction of Interstate 80 and State Route 174 between Sacramento and Lake Tahoe. Annual budgeted revenues are $6 million; the city has 11 full-time employees with one position vacant, plus 1 part-time/seasonal/contract employee; the fiscal-year end is June 30. The town was originally inhabited by the Maidu and Miwok peoples, gained prominence during the Gold Rush era, was named after Schuyler Colfax, and retains landmarks such as the restored 1905 Southern Pacific Railroad depot and a downtown of local shops and events.

The RFP comprises the primary RFP document, any attachments, and any addenda issued prior to contract award. All attachments and addenda released in relation to this RFP before any contract award are incorporated by reference.

The RFP is issued by the City of Colfax, which states it will make every effort to adhere to the schedule. Key dates: RFP issued July 1, 2025; Respondents submit written questions by July 31, 2025; City of Colfax provides responses to questions on its website www.colfax-ca.gov by August 14, 2025; Respondents submit proposals by August 28, 2025. Finalists are notified September 11, 2025; virtual finalists' interviews (if needed) with Finalists and Colfax on September 25, 2025; selection and contract award by City of Colfax on October 22, 2025.

Respondents may seek clarification of the RFP documents and must submit questions by the due date specified in Section 2.2. Written inquiries must be emailed to accounting@colfax-ca.gov with the subject line "Accounting Software Proposal Questions," and must refer to the relevant RFP section. Questions received before the submission deadline, the City's responses, and any additional terms will be posted as an addendum on the City's website www.colfax-ca.gov; the addendum becomes part of the RFP. Only written material in an Addendum is considered authoritative and binding; informal or oral communications from City personnel are not official, and the City is bound only by the RFP and formal Addenda.

The City of Colfax urges all potential respondents to read the full RFP document and attachments before responding. Respondents bear all costs for preparing and submitting proposals or participating in interviews; the City will not reimburse these costs. The City will keep confidential trade secrets hidden as allowed by law; each page containing such information must be labeled "CONFIDENTIAL" at the top and bottom with the specific trade secret information enclosed. Cost information cannot be marked as confidential, and confidential markings must be limited as much as possible.

The chunk is section 2.5 DEFINITIONS, ACRONYMS AND ABBREVIATIONS of the RFP issued by the City of Colfax. It defines: CITY as City of Colfax; CONTRACT as an agreement for services over a specified period at an agreed price; CONTRACT LEAD as the City of Colfax representative who coordinates with Respondents for contracting and manages the contract; RFP as Request for Proposals; PROPOSAL as a submission from a Respondent in response to the RFP; QUALIFIED PROPOSAL as a compliant proposal from a responsible Respondent meeting RFP requirements; RESPONDENT as an entity submitting a response (e.g., supplier, company, firm, partnership, individual). IMPLEMENTATION is defined as the timeframe for installation, including planning, development, execution, and monitoring until software is fully operational, including expansions.

Respondents must read the Instructions, the City's terms and conditions, all relevant exhibits and attachments, and any other RFP components, and comply with all requirements and specifications; they must also obtain and comply with all addenda and other changes issued in connection with the RFP. A copy of the City's standard contract with terms and conditions is available upon request. Questions, issues or exceptions regarding any term, condition, instruction or other RFP component must be submitted as questions per Section 2.3 Proposal Questions; if the City decides changes will be made, they will be communicated via an RFP addendum, and the City may leave open later negotiation and amendment of specific contract provisions addressed during the question-and-answer period. The City rejects and will not evaluate or consider any additional or modified terms and conditions or instructions submitted with a Respondent's proposal, including language that renders the proposal non-binding or subject to further negotiation; noncompliance with or any attempt to alter or delete this paragraph is sufficient grounds to reject the proposal as nonresponsive.

The chunk sets a proposal-submission rule: noncompliance with, or any attempt to alter or delete, this paragraph is sufficient grounds to reject a Respondent's proposal as nonresponsive. Respondents wanting modification of the solicitation's terms and conditions are urged to inquire during the question period per Section 2.3 whether specific proposed language is acceptable to or will be considered by the City. Objections or exceptions to the City's terms and conditions stated in the proposal itself shall not be allowed and shall be disregarded or the proposal rejected. By submitting a proposal, the Respondent understands and agrees the City may exercise discretion not to consider any and all proposed modifications.

The City will evaluate all qualified proposals submitted by the due date; selection is based on the criteria in Section 3.4: Evaluation Criteria. The goal is to award a contract to a single respondent for all items, but the City may make separate awards for different items, not award certain items, or cancel the RFP entirely. The City reserves the right to waive minor informalities or technicalities in received proposals.

From proposal submission to contract award, respondents (including representatives, sub-contractors, and suppliers) must not communicate with anyone inside or outside relevant agencies or private entities about their own or others' proposals or qualifications. Violation of this rule leads to disqualification unless the City deems the communication harmless and unintentional and in the City's best interest. Exceptions are authorized communications by the issuing agency and general inquiries before submission and after status updates.

The City shall review all proposals to confirm they meet the RFP's specifications and requirements; only qualified proposals are sent to the selection committee for evaluation. The City reserves the right to reject any proposal on the basis of fit, form, and function as well as cost, and all information furnished in the proposal may be used in determining contract award. Qualified proposals are assessed according to the evaluation criteria listed in Section 3.4: Evaluation Criteria. The City will rank all qualified proposals and may select a finalist group of Respondents to interview with City leadership, or may make a final selection without a finalist interview; finalists may be asked for additional formal responses or submissions for clarification, but the City is not required to request clarification. Price proposals cannot be altered or modified as part of clarification.

Price proposals cannot be altered or modified as part of clarification. After the evaluation process, the City will make award(s) based on the evaluation and notify Respondents via email. Award to one Respondent does not mean other proposals lacked merit; the selected proposal was deemed most advantageous and the best value to the City, all factors considered. All Respondents will be notified of the status of their qualified proposal by the date of the proposed contract award in the schedule.

The City will assess submissions based on the Respondent's overall capabilities, experience, and information provided in each response; Respondents found technically unqualified or whose submission is deemed noncompliant will not be considered. Consultants responding to this RFP will be evaluated using four weighted criteria: 45% Response to project goals and scope; 25% Technical support during software implementation and ongoing; 20% Fee proposal and implementation schedule; 10% Information, qualifications, and references.

The RFP serves two purposes: (1) to inform potential respondents of the requirements and parameters of the software solution sought by the City, and (2) to set forth the terms of the resulting contract in conjunction with other specified documents. All terms in the RFP are enforceable as contract conditions in line with the General Contract Terms and Conditions; phrases such as "shall," "must," and "requirements" establish binding contractual obligations. When evaluating or rejecting proposals, the City will consider the extent to which respondents' solutions address the City's needs as outlined in the RFP. Unless explicitly stated otherwise, no single requirement automatically disqualifies a respondent, but non-compliance with any individual requirement may lead the City to exercise its discretion to reject a proposal in its entirety.

Section 4.0 of the RFP covers proposal requirements and the procedure for submitting proposals in response to the RFP. By submitting a proposal, the Respondent agrees to meet all requirements in this section plus any other specifications, requirements, and terms and conditions stated in the RFP. Respondents with questions about a requirement or specification, or who believe modifying a requirement could improve the proposal to the City, are encouraged to submit these items as questions during the question and answer period per Section 2.3.

Proposal format rules: one (1) signed original hard copy plus one (1) digital version (e.g., Adobe Acrobat PDF); proposals must not exceed 20 pages, with an additional two (2) pages allowed for the cover letter and five (5) pages for appendices. Proposals must be organized in the specified order, with content requirements detailed in Section 4.2 (PROPOSAL CONTENTS). Digital copy and all attachments must be emailed to accounting@colfax-ca.gov by August 28, 2025, at 4:00 PM PST with subject line "Accounting and Financial Software Submission". Original hard copy must be received by the same deadline at Attn: Shanna Stahl, City of Colfax, PO Box 702, Colfax, CA 95713 (USPS) or 33 S. Main Street, Colfax, CA 95713 (other delivery). Late proposals will not be considered or evaluated, and FAX submissions will not be accepted; the Respondent is responsible for timely electronic submission and hard copy receipt.

Proposals submitted by facsimile (FAX) will not be accepted. Addenda may be added to the RFP; Respondents should regularly check the City's website at www.colfax-ca.gov for issued addenda before the proposal deadline, and all Respondents are considered to have read and understood all RFP information and addenda. Proposals may be withdrawn in writing by the office issuing the RFP before the proposal opening time stated on the cover page (or later if specified in an addendum); withdrawal requests must be on the Respondent's letterhead signed by an authorized agent. Withdrawals after proposal opening are allowed only for good cause and at the City's discretion.

Section 4.2 "Proposal Contents" of the RFP requires respondents' proposals to include the required elements outlined in the RFP. Proposals must populate all attachments of this RFP that require information. An authorized signature must be included where requested. Additional details required for each proposal section are stated to be included below.

Tab 1 of the proposal requires respondents to address their approach to meeting the proposal goals and producing the deliverables outlined in Section 5.0, and encourages suggestions to improve implementation and utilization of the software and technical support approach. Specific required elements: submission of a completed "Software Abilities and Requirements" spreadsheet included as Attachment F; identification of the types of licenses offered for different levels of use; description of account number customization abilities; identification of where/when additional applications or other vendors will be utilized to meet requirements; and an outline of the availability of virtual demos to view product capabilities.

Tab 2 of the proposal requires Respondents to describe their proposed strategy and technical approach to meet the scope of work requirements in Section 5. Required elements: an implementation plan and timeline for execution, with the City's goal of going live on July 1, 2026, in coordination with the new fiscal year; description of levels of support for implementation; description of levels of support for recurring licenses and services; identification of key personnel for implementation; identification of training for software for different license levels, indicating whether training is in person, virtual, or standard recordings; and description of the proposed client engagement approach, including the use of an account manager.

The chunk is part of Tab 3: Firm Information and Qualifications under Section 4.2 Proposal Contents. It states that if multiple firms are responding as a team, the required firm information shall be listed for each company.

Tab 3.1 Organization Information of the proposal requires: firm name, address, phone, website, and primary contact name, title and contact information; firm history, state of organization or incorporation, number of full-time employees, and type of ownership; hours of operation project managers will be available for technical assistance; office location(s) (City, State) from which key team individuals will operate. Proposers must also describe how their firm or team responds to the City's desire for participation by businesses owned by minorities, women, disabled, disabled business enterprises, and small businesses.

Tab 3.2 "Firm Qualifications and Experience" requires respondents to include recent relevant experience with project location and description, key staff who worked on the projects, and how results or effectiveness were measured. Required experience areas: implementing accounting and financial software for local governments, regional councils of government, or other federal grant-funded organizations; advising clients on streamlining procedures to improve organizational efficiency; and providing continued support for improvements and/or daily operations. Respondents must complete and submit Attachment B: References Sheet (may be recreated if content remains unchanged). If possible, the City prefers at least one local referral available for an in-person software demonstration.

Tab 3.3 requires a summary of qualifications for key personnel and any subcontractors proposed to provide services to the City under the proposed scope of work. Attachment A (Pricing Proposal) must state the total cost to the City for all services including materials, supplies and travel; the City will not accept unlimited reimbursable expenses, so any reimbursable expenses must be capped in the price proposal. Attachment A serves as a cover sheet, with the price proposal format at the Respondent's discretion but referencing the specific tasks and deliverables in Section 5, including: implementation fee and recurring fees broken out in detail; breakout of license fees; additional fees for support services with costs during implementation separated from post-implementation; and estimate of costs/fees for additional applications and/or vendors. Attachment B (References) requires a minimum of three (3) references for similar services, with valid e-mail addresses, and failure to provide a valid email may subject the proposal to rejection. Attachment C (Location of Workers Utilized by Respondent) requires detailing the location(s) where performance will occur and how resources or workers outside the United States will be utilized, which the City will evaluate for additional risks, costs and other factors before making an award. Attachment D is a Certification of Financial Condition.

The RFP requires several attachments with the proposal: Attachment D, Certification of Financial Condition, by which each Respondent certifies it is financially stable and able to complete the scope of work, and must notify the City within thirty (30) days of any occurrence or condition materially altering the truth of the certification from the date of Certification to Contract expiration. Attachment E, Certificate of Insurance, requires proof of insurance for the type of work solicited, including but not limited to workers compensation and commercial general liability coverage. Attachment F, Software Abilities and Requirements, requires completing an attached Excel spreadsheet (a separate document provided by the City) and returning it with the submission. Attachment G, Software Application Requirements, requires documentation demonstrating measures in place for protecting financial data and the secure access controls implemented.

The chunk states that Respondents shall note the requirements of Respondents to this RFP and fully review the standard City contract for services. It references a standard City contract for services as a document Respondents must review. No further details, numbers, dates or amounts are given.

Section 5.0 is titled "SCOPE OF WORK EXPECTATIONS" and states that the scope of work outlines expected deliverables to aid Respondents in preparing their RFP submissions. Required items must be included in the response; optional items are noted as optional. The City welcomes suggestions to enhance the final product.

The scope of work is organized into four tasks. Task 1 (Approach & Project Management Plan) requires weekly meetings for progress, budget and timeline monitoring, a personnel management plan with a dedicated project manager and technical staff, understanding of auditing and reporting requirements for software implementation, and a recommended account structure for auditable reporting. Task 2 (Software Installation & Implementation) requires assistance with financial report writing, import of the prior 5 years of data for history, collaboration with Accounting and IT to minimize disruptions, and reduced downtime and operational impacts during transition. Task 3 (Staff Training During Implementation) requires personalized training and manuals for power users, support for the first 12 months post-implementation, and at least 1 recorded training session and manual for all staff. Task 4 (Ongoing Technical Assistance & Support) requires automated updates and software change communications, support for annual e-filing such as 1099s and W-2s, and a help desk or ticketing system for support prioritization.

The City plans to start the project soon after awarding the contract and finalizing negotiations. The goal is to complete implementation by July 1, 2026, for the new fiscal year. Respondents should provide a proposed timeline and task sequence based on their expertise.

Attachment A is the Pricing Proposal (16 pages). Respondents must submit a detailed price proposal for the scope of services in the RFP, with the format left to the respondent's discretion. The City cannot accept unlimited reimbursable expenses; proposed reimbursable expenses must be capped. Three blank fields are provided: Total price for all services and deliverables, Total reimbursable expenses cap, and Total price proposal. The price proposal must detail the specific tasks and deliverables identified in Section 5.

Attachment B: References requires the respondent to provide at least three (3) references for whom similar services have been performed as outlined herein. E-mail addresses must be valid; failure to provide a valid email address may result in rejection of the respondent's proposal. The form provides three reference blocks (Reference 1, Reference 2, Reference 3), each collecting Client Name, Type of Service / Scope of Work, Performance Dates, Contact Name, Phone, and Email.

Attachment C ("Location of Workers Utilized by Respondent") requires the Respondent to specify the location(s) where performance of work will take place and to describe how it plans to use resources or workers outside of the United States for this contract. The City will assess the risks, costs, and other factors related to this utilization before making an award decision. Respondents must answer whether any work under the Contract will be performed outside the United States (Yes/No); if Yes, they must list the locations outside the United States where work will be conducted by the Respondent, sub-contractors, employees or other personnel, and describe the corporate structure and locations of corporate employees and activities of the Respondent, its affiliates or sub-contractors executing work outside the United States. The Respondent agrees to provide written notice to the City regarding relocation of the Respondent, its employees, sub-contractors or other personnel to locations outside the United States, and must identify all locations within the United States where performance will take place.

Attachment D is a "Certification of Financial Condition" form to be completed by the Respondent, including the Name of Respondent and checkboxes certifying stable financial condition and an unqualified audit opinion on the latest audit (with a field for Date of latest audit), no outstanding liabilities to the Internal Revenue Service or any other government entity including tax and judgment liens, current on federal and state taxes and required employment-related contributions and withholdings, no ongoing litigation or findings of noncompliance under federal or state law, and no past or current litigation or findings of noncompliance that may affect ability to meet the requirements of this Contract. The undersigned must be authorized to make these statements on behalf of the Respondent. The certification remains valid and the Respondent must notify the Contract Lead within 15 days of any material changes to the representations; any unchecked box requires an explanation. The form requires Signature, Date, Printed Name and Title, and must be signed by an individual authorized to represent the Respondent.

The chunk is from "ATTACHMENT E: CERTIFICATION OF INSURANCE" of the City of Colfax RFP. Respondents must provide proof of insurance for this RFP's work. The required coverage includes workers compensation and commercial general liability.

The chunk is from "ATTACHMENT F: SOFTWARE ABILITIES AND REQUIREMENTS" (pages 21) of the City of Colfax RFP. Respondents must complete the attached Excel spreadsheet and return it with their submission. The spreadsheet is a separate document to be provided by the City.
